title: Emergency basics
description: Water, food, and staying safe during outages.

cards.title: Build a three-day kit
cards.summary: Plan for each person's water, shelf-stable food, light, information, medicines, and essential documents. Adjust for children, pets, and local hazards.
steps: Store at least one gallon (3.8 L) of water per person per day for three days.
Add three days of nonperishable food and a manual can opener.
Include a flashlight, spare batteries, radio, first-aid supplies, medicines, and local maps.
Write a household contact and meeting plan; keep a portable copy.

cards.title: When drinking water may be unsafe
cards.summary: Follow local advisories. Bottled water is the first choice; boiling can kill germs when officials say to boil water. Boiling does not remove chemical contamination.
steps: Check official local water notices when a connection is available.
Use bottled water for drinking, food preparation, and brushing teeth if advised.
For a boil-water advisory, bring clear water to a rolling boil for one minute (three minutes above 6,500 ft); cool before use.
If fuel, chemicals, or radiation may contaminate water, do not rely on boiling; use a safe alternate source.

cards.title: Power outage priorities
cards.summary: Keep food cold, light the space safely, and keep generators outside to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.
steps: Keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed as much as possible.
Use battery lights instead of candles where possible.
Run a portable generator outside, far from windows, doors, and vents; never in a garage or home.
Keep phones charged with a safe battery pack and check local alerts when service returns.
cards.source: FoodSafety.gov disaster food safety; ESFI portable generators
